messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: decode-asia-1 pool reporting elevated OOMs (12 OOMs in 4m). Multiple pods restarted. Investigate: https://ops.redwood.internal/incidents/4620001111
Noah (oncall): Paged. Looking now. Any customer-facing errors?
Zara (SRE): LB shows aborted /v1/stream sessions and container exit code 137. Kube logs show large KV allocations. Sample: 
Owen (runtime): ```
2026-03-15T18:14:22Z decode-pod-3 PID 1982 killed by OOM
model=dec-13b seq_len=8192 tokens_streamed=unbounded kv_growth=high
CUDA: out of memory in attention_kernel
```
Zara (SRE): Correlating with a recent edge sanitizer rollout ~25m ago that normalizes headers. Some TLS rewrap paths appear to strip `x-client-max-tokens` -> clients fall back to server defaults (unset) -> runaway generation.
Priya (edge): Confirmed — edge change removed unknown headers by default on rewrap. Rolling back now. Canary shows header preserved after revert.
Noah (oncall): We need immediate containment to stop OOMs while rollback propagates. Options?
Owen (runtime): Containment plan (executing):
1) toggle pool streaming off: `redwoodctl pool update decode-asia-1 --streaming=false`
2) set cluster env: `REDWOOD_STREAM_SOFT_MAX=512` (forces soft stop token)
3) enable model-fallback: route to dec-quant-7b when node_mem>70%
4) evict long streams > 60s
Applying step 1 & 2 now.
Hank (support): Customer impact: logs show ~1.5k failed streams in last 15m, 4 affected tenants; enterprise-acct-99 ~600 failed sessions. Drafting holding message.
Zara (SRE): After soft cap and pool disable, OOM rate down to ~2/min from 12/min. Some older containers still restart due to cached long-lived streams; eviction running.
Priya (edge): Rollback complete and canary OK. Will add integration test for TLS rewrap header preservation.
Owen (runtime): Evict command: 
```bash
kubectl -n decode exec deploy/stream-evictor -- ./evict --age=60s --label=pool=decode-asia-1
```
Also adding allocator pre-check to avoid large attention allocs if remaining RAM < threshold. PR incoming.
Marta (product): Need an internal summary for status page: short blurb + ETA for full fix. Any numbers for ETA?
Hank (support): Suggest message: "We experienced elevated error rates for streaming endpoints due to an internal header normalization change which removed client token limits for some traffic. We have contained the issue by rolling back the change and applying temporary server-side limits. We will follow up with a root-cause and timeline within 48 hours."
Noah (oncall): Handoff plan: I'll document timeline and hand to Zara for postmortem. Action owners: Zara - verification & postmortem, Owen - runtime fixes (soft-stop + allocator guard), Priya - gateway tests & canary, Hank - customer comms, Marta - product impact summary.
incident-bot: Incident state: contained. Severity S2. Reminder: create postmortem within 72h and attach logs/heapdumps.
Zara (SRE): Timeline notes: 18:09 edge sanitizer deployed; 18:14 first OOM alert; 18:15 oncall paged; 18:16 rollback started; 18:17 pool streaming disabled & soft cap applied; 18:19 eviction started; 18:22 OOM rate subsided but residual restarts until 18:28.
Owen (runtime): Follow-ups: implement hard guard in allocator, server-side default max_tokens for streams, emit telemetry for streams missing x-client-max-tokens, test harness to simulate long-kv growth. I'll file PRs today.
Priya (edge): I'll add a canary that simulates TLS rewrap preserving headers and add to CI.
Hank (support): Sending initial customer notices now. Will include tenant-specific failure counts and mitigation steps.
Marta (product): Please include latency and cost delta for fallback model in postmortem.
Noah (oncall): Handing off to Zara. Logging out. :wave:
